question: Will a federal grand jury in Washington, D.C. have returned and publicly disclosed an indictment against James Comey over his 2016 disclosure to The New York Times by November 13, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of Nov 3, no D.C. indictment, no-bill, or ruling reported. DOJ filed a criminal information because it could not secure an indictment before the Oct 5, 2026 limitations deadline. Two prior DOJ probes of the leak declined to charge, and the key witness (Richman) contradicted the theory. D.C. grand juries have repeatedly refused politically sensitive indictments, including Hutchinson on Oct 27. On the other side, DOJ says it is actively presenting, has new post-2016 evidence, faces Speedy Trial pressure around Nov 5, and has indicted Comey twice before. An indictment that folds in the 2016 conduct as part of a broader conspiracy would still count. No human market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:

It used an information because no indictment was obtained before the 10-year statute of limitations ran (CNN/NPR, Oct 30, 2026).
- Comey did not waive indictment and moved to dismiss as time-barred. The government says an information tolls the limitations clock (CBS/The Hill, Oct 2026).
- Oct 30, 2026 hearing: McFadden did not rule and floated waiting to see whether DOJ gets an indictment. He said an indictment was 'no sure thing' and that 'ham sandwiches are harder to indict these days' (AP via KSL, Oct 30).
- Prosecutor Farahnak: 'We are still going to the grand jury very diligently' and 'They may indict, they may not indict.' DOJ cites new evidence of acts after Oct 2016, up to April 2017, and may add charges (CNN, Spokesman/Bloomberg, Oct 30).
- AP/ABC: Nov 5, 2026 may technically be the last day to seek an indictment before the information is dismissed under the Speedy Trial Act (the exact mechanics are disputed in coverage).
- Two prior DOJ investigations of these leaks ended without charges (CNN, Oct 30). In earlier 2025 reporting, Daniel Richman told the FBI Comey never asked him to talk to the media, and prosecutors called him a hostile witness (ABC News, 2025). Richman was subpoenaed by a grand jury in the renewed probe (CNN, Aug 31, 2026).
- A D.C. grand jury declined to indict Cassidy Hutchinson on Oct 27, 2026. D.C. grand juries have repeatedly returned no-bills in politically sensitive cases in 2025-26. On Nov 2, 2026, a magistrate tossed a complaint against ex-FBI officials Floris and Benavides, calling it 'weaponization' (unrelated conduct).
- Counter-evidence: grand juries in Virginia indicted Comey in Sept 2025 (false statements) and Apr 2026 ('86 47' post). Grand juries return indictments in the overwhelming majority of ordinary presentments.
- Status quo: no indictment. As of the Nov 3 searches, no report of a return, a no-bill, or a ruling on dismissal.

calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) whether anything happened Nov 1-3: four searches found no report of an indictment, no-bill, or ruling, so the status quo holds. (2) The 30-day no-indictment agreement: CBS confirms that per Comey's filings DOJ agreed not to seek an indictment for 30 days after an early-October emergency hearing, ending early November. That likely delays a vote to about Nov 5-8 but leaves ~a week in the window. (3) The exact Speedy Trial deadline is still unsettled; AP's 'may technically be Nov 5' is the best available, and either way it pushes toward a vote soon. (4) The grand jury's propensity is pure judgment: recent D.C. no-bills against prior declinations by DOJ/Durham, versus Espionage Act framing and Comey's prior indictments. I take ~0.7-0.75 on a vote in the window times ~0.35-0.4 on a true bill, giving ~0.26. That sits nearer runs 1 and 3; run 2 underweights the pressure on DOJ to seek a vote. No market found.
